key_insight: Increasing cylinder rotation suppresses conventional vortex shedding before unsteadiness re-emerges at high rotation as intermittent, multiscale flow.
engineering_relevance: Rotation offers a means to control wake dynamics and lift, but non-monotonic drag and renewed unsteadiness complicate operating-point selection.
method: 130 high-fidelity, two-dimensional compressible-flow simulations at Re∞ = 3800 and M∞ = 0.1.
Rotation-rate sweep over 0.1 ≤ Ω ≤ 10 with surface-pressure, skin-friction, and aerodynamic-force analysis.
Vorticity-based proper orthogonal decomposition to characterize coherent flow structures.
evidence_signal: The simulations identify a suppression transition around Ω = 2.2–2.8, followed at higher rotation by renewed intermittency and local Mach numbers approaching 0.5.
watch_item: The two-dimensional setup and fixed Reynolds and free-stream Mach numbers limit direct extrapolation to three-dimensional engineering flows.
paper_title: Rotation-driven suppression and re-emergence of unsteady flow past a circular cylinder
